Without `--root`, `bind` records the nearest ancestor of the profile that holds a `.git` entry; when none exists, `bind` exits 2 naming `--root`.

The binding gains a `root` key under binding schema 2 (`crates/model/src/binding.rs`). A schema 1 binding stays readable by every command with today's behavior (`--root` required). `bind` with the same profile and machine id on a schema 1 binding rewrites it as schema 2 with `root` (an in-place upgrade under the writer lock, journaled). A different profile or machine id stays `E_REBIND_UNSUPPORTED`.

On every command that takes `--root`, the flag is optional. The default is the binding's `root`. An explicit `--root` wins. With neither, the command exits 2 naming `bind --root`. The plan digest for the same tree is identical whether the root came from the flag or from the binding.

changes.required_detail: Define leaf completion as a nonempty, valid canonical criterion set whose markers are all checked. A missing expected criterion fails closed. Do not automatically check criteria merely because evidence or a status appears.

changes.reason: Stable IDs are necessary. Current acceptance entries combine independent outcomes, tests and human approvals. One checkbox for an entire compound entry can conceal which requirement remains open.
changes.required_detail: Split independently satisfiable obligations, especially owner approval versus technical evidence, while preserving original wording and all constraints. Keep explanatory examples and prohibitions with their outcome when they are not separate accomplishments. Map every original entry to its resulting IDs. Allocate new IDs monotonically; never renumber surviving IDs or reuse removed IDs.

changes.reason: Fresh child-checkbox derivation avoids duplicate state, but current epic goals are requirements without explicit criterion mapping. A relation alone does not prove that every epic requirement is checkable.
changes.required_detail: Map each epic goal clause to linked canonical child criterion IDs. Add any uncovered epic requirement to an appropriate child as a real unchecked criterion. Display task completion as the all-criteria predicate; display epic completion as the all-expected-child predicate. Link each epic requirement to the checkbox that can be edited. Do not create editable task or epic summary checkboxes. If the user requires a literal independently editable task-level checkbox, this design needs clarification because that introduces a second completion state.

changes.reason: Fresh live reads and ID preservation are necessary but not sufficient to prevent overwriting edits made between read and write. Changed text can also invalidate checked criteria accidentally.
changes.required_detail: Use a conditional write or version check if available. Otherwise perform a narrow criterion migration, re-read immediately before writing, stop on differences, and verify persisted state afterward. This reduces but cannot eliminate a race without conditional writes; report that limitation. Preserve a checked marker only when its obligation is unchanged. Reopen materially changed obligations with a recorded reason. Pure formatting or typo corrections must not reopen work. Never write snapshot descriptions over live descriptions.

changes.reason: Verify native checkbox persistence before treating markdown rendering as a usable state mechanism. Preserve human authorization requirements. No daemon or separate tracker is needed.
changes.required_detail: Confirm a checkbox can be edited, saved and read back as its canonical persisted marker, including after reload. Use a clearly labeled temporary test criterion if a production criterion must not be falsely checked. Remove the test afterward and verify the original markers. Verify all updated criteria remain editable; do not infer this from rendered checkbox glyphs alone.

Keep operational readiness separate from completion. Prerequisite completion reads canonical checkboxes; exact-plan authorization and current evidence remain separate dispatch gates.

changes.reason: Persisted acceptance markers can provide the sole completion state without discarding evidence or independent execution authority. Existing status in-review on DFM-13 demonstrates why status cannot define completion.

Status, labels, comments, PR state and snapshot metadata do not establish completion. Evidence and applicable owner approvals must support each check. A checked prerequisite does not authorize implementation, device changes, merge, cleanup or publication.

changes.reason: Stable IDs support preservation, but a long bundled criterion can hide unmet obligations. Split only outcomes that can pass or fail independently. Preserve safety constraints next to the action they constrain.
changes.wording: Assign immutable DFM-N.Cnn IDs to acceptance criteria. Each criterion names a verifiable outcome and preserves its scope, constraints and required evidence. Split independent outcomes when one can pass while another fails. Do not create separate completion boxes for every prohibition, command argument or evidence field. Retired IDs are never reused.

changes.reason: Child-only rollup must retain all epic goal obligations. Linking all children is insufficient unless the requirement map covers every epic goal. No duplicate persisted epic or leaf summary checkbox is needed.
changes.wording: An epic is complete exactly when its expected current children are present, each child has a valid nonempty canonical acceptance checklist, every child criterion is checked, and every epic goal obligation is mapped to those criteria. Show child links and read-only derived completion totals. Do not store a second epic completion checklist. If any expected child, description or criterion cannot be read, treat the epic as incomplete. Re-read prerequisites before dispatch; all canonical criteria must be checked.

changes.reason: Preservation by ID is necessary but insufficient when scope, dependencies, shared source or evidence identity changes. Blind whole-description writes can erase checks made after a read.
changes.wording: Before revision, read the live canonical description. Preserve checked markers only for unchanged criteria whose evidence remains applicable. Reopen a changed criterion with a recorded reason; add new criteria unchecked. Reconcile affected criteria after shared-source, scope or evidence changes using the existing evidence-refresh rule. Never restore checkbox state from a snapshot. If the description changes during editing, stop that write, reread and reconcile instead of overwriting it. Check criterion IDs and markers again after persistence.

changes.reason: Native description checklist persistence is the smallest mechanism. A disposable or newly added unchecked criterion can test editing without falsely checking an existing requirement.
changes.wording: Verify native checkbox editing and persistence through save, reload and fresh description read-back. Use a disposable test task or an explicit test-only criterion; do not briefly mark a real unmet requirement complete. Verify checked and unchecked transitions, exact criterion text and IDs, and preservation of unrelated content. Remove only the disposable test artifact. Add no tracker, daemon or automatic status synchronization.

Keep completion of the preserved validation run, exact-SHA hosted checks and PR metadata individually checkable. PR remaining open is compatible with completion. Merge authorization remains separate.

Final owner acceptance remains a mandatory checked criterion supported by explicit acceptance evidence. Reconcile every requirement to canonical criterion IDs. Publishing documentation cannot imply release, visibility or deployment authority.
